facts.std: The red flesh of a strawberry is a swollen part of the flower base; each tiny 'seed' on its surface is actually a separate fruit.

facts.ja: わさびの辛みは、すりおろした直後が最も強く、時間がたつと飛んで弱くなる。
facts.easy: Wasabi is hottest right after you make it. The hot taste goes away after a while.
facts.std: Freshly grated wasabi is at its most pungent right away; its sharp flavor fades as the compounds evaporate over several minutes.

facts.ja: 約3800年前のメソポタミアには、ビールづくりの歌（ニンカシ讃歌）が残っている。最古級のレシピのひとつとされる。
facts.easy: A song from about 3,800 years ago tells how to make beer. It is one of the oldest cooking notes in the world.
facts.std: The Hymn to Ninkasi, written in Mesopotamia about 3,800 years ago, describes beer brewing and is one of the oldest known recipes.

facts.ja: 英語の salary（給料）は、ラテン語の sal（塩）に由来する。ただし「兵士の給料が塩で払われた」という話ははっきりした証拠がない。
facts.easy: The English word salary comes from the Latin word for salt. But the story that soldiers were paid in salt may not be true.
facts.std: The word 'salary' comes from Latin sal, meaning salt, although the popular story that Roman soldiers were paid in salt lacks firm evidence.

facts.ja: 人の遺伝子の約60%は、バナナにも似た働きをする遺伝子がある。生き物の基本のしくみは共通している。
facts.easy: Many of our genes have a similar gene in bananas. All living things share some basic parts.
facts.std: About 60% of human genes have a recognizable counterpart in the banana genome, a reminder that life shares basic machinery.

facts.ja: パイナップルにはブロメラインという酵素が入っていて、肉をやわらかくする。食べると舌がピリピリするのもこのため。
facts.easy: Pineapple can make meat soft. That is also why your tongue can feel strange when you eat a lot of it.
facts.std: Pineapple contains bromelain, an enzyme that breaks down protein, which is why it tenderizes meat and can make your tongue tingle.

facts.ja: 学習のあとにカフェインをとると、記憶の定着を助ける可能性を示した研究がある。
facts.easy: One study found that coffee after learning may help you remember things better.
facts.std: A 2014 study found that caffeine taken after studying images helped people remember them better a day later.

facts.ja: セルビアのロバのミルクで作るチーズ「プレ」は世界一高価なチーズのひとつで、1kgで約1000ユーロ（約16万円）する。
facts.easy: A cheese made from donkey milk in Serbia is one of the most expensive cheeses in the world.
facts.std: Pule, a Serbian cheese made from donkey milk, is among the world's most expensive, selling for around 1,000 euros per kilogram.

facts.ja: 人類が農業を始めたのは約1万年前。それより前の長い歴史のほとんどは狩りと採集の暮らしだった。
facts.easy: People started farming about 10,000 years ago. Before that, people hunted animals and picked plants for food.
facts.std: Humans began farming about 10,000 years ago; for most of our history before that, people lived as hunter-gatherers.

facts.ja: ブルーベリーの青紫色はアントシアニンという色素によるもの。ポリフェノールの一種。
facts.easy: Blueberries get their blue color from a natural color called anthocyanin.
facts.std: Blueberries owe their deep blue color to anthocyanins, a group of plant pigments.

facts.ja: 「うま味」は1908年に日本の池田菊苗が見つけた。2000年代に舌の受容体が見つかり、5番目の基本味として広く認められた。
facts.easy: Umami was found by a Japanese scientist in 1908. Today it is called the fifth basic taste.
facts.std: Umami was identified by Japanese chemist Kikunae Ikeda in 1908 and became widely accepted as the fifth basic taste after taste receptors for it were found in the 2000s.

facts.ja: 砂糖がぜいたく品からふだんの食品になったのは、17〜18世紀のカリブ海の植民地での大量生産から。その裏には奴隷労働の歴史がある。
facts.easy: Sugar was once a luxury. It became common after it was grown in large amounts in the Caribbean, often by slaves.
facts.std: Sugar turned from luxury into everyday food in the 17th and 18th centuries through plantations in the Caribbean, which depended on enslaved labor.

facts.ja: 卵には人に必要なアミノ酸がそろっていて「完全栄養食」とも呼ばれる。ただしビタミンCは含まない。
facts.easy: Eggs have almost everything your body needs, but they have no vitamin C.
facts.std: Eggs contain all the essential amino acids and many vitamins, but they have no vitamin C.

facts.ja: にせの薬だと知らされていても、効果を感じることがある（オープンラベル・プラセボ）という研究がある。
facts.easy: Some people feel better even when they know their medicine is not real.
facts.std: Studies of 'open-label placebos' suggest some people feel better even when told their pills contain no active drug.

facts.ja: 夢中になって時間を忘れる「フロー」の状態では、力を最大限に発揮しやすい。心理学者チクセントミハイが名づけた。
facts.easy: When you are fully into an activity and forget the time, it is called 'flow'. People often do their best work then.
facts.std: In a state of 'flow', people become so absorbed that they lose track of time and often perform at their best; the term was coined by Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi.

facts.ja: 「つり橋効果」：揺れる橋の上のドキドキを、相手への好意と取り違えることがあるという有名な実験がある。
facts.easy: A famous study found that people on a shaking bridge may mistake their fast heartbeat for love.
facts.std: A famous 1974 experiment suggested that people on a frightening suspension bridge may mistake their racing heart for attraction.

facts.ja: ツァイガルニク効果：終わっていない作業は、終わった作業より思い出しやすいとされる。ドラマの「続く」が気になるのもこのため。
facts.easy: We often remember unfinished tasks better than finished ones. That is why we want to know what happens next in a TV drama.
facts.std: The Zeigarnik effect suggests people remember unfinished tasks better than completed ones, one reason cliffhangers keep us watching.

facts.ja: ダニング＝クルーガー効果：ある分野に不慣れな人ほど自分の力を高く見積もり、得意な人ほど低く見積もりがち。
facts.easy: People who are new to something often think they are better than they are. Experts often think they are worse.
facts.std: The Dunning-Kruger effect describes how people with little skill in an area tend to overestimate it, while experts tend to underestimate theirs.

facts.ja: ピグマリオン効果：期待をかけられた人は、その期待に近い成果を出しやすいという考え。
facts.easy: When people expect a lot from you, you may do better. This is called the Pygmalion effect.
facts.std: The Pygmalion effect is the idea that higher expectations from others can lead people to perform better.

facts.ja: 作業が中断されると、元の作業に集中し直すまでに平均20分以上かかるという研究がある。
facts.easy: A study found that after you stop work to do something else, it can take over 20 minutes to get back to it.
facts.std: Research on office workers found that after an interruption it took on average over 20 minutes to return to the original task.

facts.ja: 24時間眠らずにいると、判断力は血中アルコール濃度0.1%で酔ったときと同じくらいまで落ちるという研究がある。
facts.easy: If you stay awake for 24 hours, your mind works about as badly as if you were drunk.
facts.std: Research suggests that staying awake for 24 hours impairs performance about as much as a blood alcohol level of 0.1%.

facts.ja: テトリス効果：同じ作業を長く続けると、夢や頭の中にその動きのパターンが出てくることがある。
facts.easy: After you play a game for a long time, you may see it in your dreams. This is called the Tetris effect.
facts.std: The Tetris effect is when people who spend long periods on an activity start to see its patterns in their thoughts and dreams.

facts.ja: カラーバス効果：ある色やものを意識すると、急にそれが目につくようになる。
facts.easy: When you start to think about the color red, you suddenly see red things everywhere.
facts.std: Once you start paying attention to something, such as a color or a car model, you suddenly notice it everywhere.

facts.ja: 確証バイアス：人は自分の考えに合う情報ばかり集めてしまいがち。
facts.easy: People like to find facts that agree with what they already believe.
facts.std: Confirmation bias is the tendency to seek out and favor information that supports what we already believe.

facts.ja: 返報性の原理：何かをもらうと、お返しをしなければと感じやすい。多くの文化に見られる心理。
facts.easy: When someone gives us something, we want to give something back. This is true in many cultures.
facts.std: The norm of reciprocity, the feeling that we should return favors, appears in cultures all over the world.

facts.ja: 大人になると時間が速く過ぎるように感じる。新しい経験が減るためという説がある。
facts.easy: Time seems to go faster as we get older. One idea is that we have fewer new experiences.
facts.std: Time often seems to speed up as we age; one explanation is that we have fewer novel experiences to mark the passing days.

facts.ja: プルースト効果：においは、昔の記憶や気持ちを強く思い出させる。
facts.easy: A smell can bring back an old memory very strongly.
facts.std: Smells can trigger vivid memories and emotions from the past, sometimes called the Proust effect.

facts.ja: 音楽を聞くと、人は自然とリズムに体を合わせようとする。
facts.easy: When we hear music, our bodies want to move with the beat.
facts.std: When people hear music, they naturally tend to synchronize their movements with the beat, a process called entrainment.

facts.ja: 系列位置効果：一覧の最初と最後の項目は、真ん中より覚えやすい。
facts.easy: In a list, it is easier to remember the first and last things than the ones in the middle.
facts.std: The serial-position effect means we tend to remember the first and last items in a list better than those in the middle.

facts.ja: 笑いは人どうしの絆を強める役割をもつと考えられている。チンパンジーなどの類人猿も遊びの中で笑う。
facts.easy: Laughing helps people feel close. Apes like chimpanzees also laugh when they play.
facts.std: Laughter is thought to help strengthen social bonds, and great apes such as chimpanzees also laugh during play.

facts.ja: 最初のコンピューターウイルスとされる「Creeper」（1971年）は、こわすためではなく実験として作られたものだった。
facts.easy: One of the first computer viruses, made in 1971, was only a test. It did not try to hurt computers.
facts.std: Creeper, often called the first computer virus, was written in 1971 as an experiment and did no damage.

facts.ja: 世界初のウェブサイトは1991年にCERNのティム・バーナーズ＝リーが公開した。今もそのページを見ることができる。
facts.easy: The first website was made in 1991. You can still visit it today.
facts.std: Tim Berners-Lee published the first website at CERN in 1991, and a copy of it is still online today.

facts.ja: 地球のまわりでは1万基以上の人工衛星が動いていて、使われなくなった衛星やかけら（宇宙ごみ）はさらに多い。
facts.easy: More than 10,000 working machines go around the Earth in space. There is even more space trash.
facts.std: More than 10,000 active satellites now orbit Earth, along with far more pieces of space debris.

facts.ja: 1947年、ハーバード大学のコンピューターに本物の虫（ガ）がはさまり、「バグ」として記録に残った。
facts.easy: In 1947, a real insect got stuck inside a computer. People wrote it down as a 'bug'.
facts.std: In 1947, engineers found a moth trapped in the Harvard Mark II computer and taped it into their log as the 'first actual case of bug being found'.

facts.ja: 電子レンジは1945年、レーダーの技術者がポケットのチョコレートが溶けたことに気づいたのがきっかけで生まれた。
facts.easy: The microwave oven was invented when an engineer saw that a chocolate bar in his pocket had melted.
facts.std: The microwave oven was invented after engineer Percy Spencer noticed that a chocolate bar in his pocket melted near radar equipment in 1945.

facts.ja: GPSはもともと軍事用の技術。1983年の大韓航空機撃墜事件のあと、民間でも使えるようにすると発表された。
facts.easy: GPS was first made for the army. After a plane was shot down in 1983, the US said everyone could use it.
facts.std: GPS began as a military system; after Korean Air Lines Flight 007 was shot down in 1983, the US announced it would be opened to civilian use.

facts.ja: 初代プレイステーションは1994年に日本で発売された。CD-ROMを使い、ゲームの表現を大きく変えた。
facts.easy: The first PlayStation came out in Japan in 1994. It used CDs and changed video games.
facts.std: The original PlayStation launched in Japan in 1994, and its use of CD-ROMs helped transform video games.

facts.ja: 1971年、レイ・トムリンソンが初めてネットワークで電子メールを送った。相手は隣に置いた別のコンピューターだった。
facts.easy: The first email was sent in 1971. It went to a computer right next to the sender.
facts.std: Ray Tomlinson sent the first network email in 1971, between two computers sitting side by side.

facts.ja: ディープラーニングの基本的な考え方は1980年代からあったが、計算機の力が足りず、広く使われたのは2010年代になってから。
facts.easy: The main ideas of deep learning were around in the 1980s. But computers were too slow to use them well until the 2010s.
facts.std: Key ideas behind deep learning existed in the 1980s, but they only took off in the 2010s, when computers became powerful enough.

facts.ja: Wi-Fiという名前には特別な意味はない。Hi-Fiに似せて作ったブランド名。
facts.easy: The name Wi-Fi does not mean anything. It was made to sound like 'hi-fi'.
facts.std: The name Wi-Fi doesn't stand for anything; it was a brand name created to sound like 'hi-fi'.

facts.ja: 合言葉（パスワード）は2000年以上前の古代ローマ軍でも使われていた。夜の見張りで仲間を見分けるため。
facts.easy: Over 2,000 years ago, Roman soldiers used secret words at night to know who was a friend.
facts.std: More than 2,000 years ago, Roman soldiers used watchwords at night to tell friend from enemy, an early form of the password.

facts.ja: Netflixは1997年、DVDを郵送で貸し出す会社として始まった。ネット配信を始めたのは2007年。
facts.easy: Netflix started in 1997 by sending DVDs by mail. It started streaming in 2007.
facts.std: Netflix was founded in 1997 as a DVD-by-mail rental service and only began streaming video in 2007.

facts.ja: リチウムイオン電池を開発した吉野彰は、2019年にノーベル化学賞を受けた。スマートフォンの普及を支えた技術。
facts.easy: Akira Yoshino helped make the battery in your phone. He won the Nobel Prize in 2019.
facts.std: Akira Yoshino shared the 2019 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for developing the lithium-ion battery, which powers today's smartphones.

facts.ja: コンピューターのマウスは1964年ごろダグラス・エンゲルバートが考えた。最初のマウスは木の箱だった。
facts.easy: The computer mouse was made in the 1960s by Douglas Engelbart. The first one was a small wooden box.
facts.std: Douglas Engelbart invented the computer mouse in the 1960s; the first prototype was a wooden box with two wheels.

facts.ja: 水泳のバタフライは、平泳ぎのルールのすき間から生まれた。腕を水の上で戻すことが禁止されていなかったため。
facts.easy: The butterfly swimming style began as a new way to do the breaststroke. The rules did not stop swimmers from moving their arms above the water.
facts.std: The butterfly stroke grew out of a loophole in breaststroke rules, which did not forbid bringing the arms forward over the water.

facts.ja: 白黒模様のサッカーボールは、1970年のW杯で白黒テレビでも見やすいように使われて広まった。
facts.easy: The black and white football became popular at the 1970 World Cup. It was easy to see on black and white TV.
facts.std: The classic black-and-white football became famous at the 1970 World Cup, partly because it was easy to see on black-and-white television.

facts.ja: テニスの点数が「15、30、40」と数えるのは、時計の文字盤から来たという説がある（はっきりとは分かっていない）。
facts.easy: Nobody is sure why tennis scores go 15, 30, 40. One idea is that they come from the face of a clock.
facts.std: No one knows for certain why tennis is scored 15, 30, 40; one popular theory links it to the quarters of a clock face.

facts.ja: バスケットボールは1891年、体育教師のジェームズ・ネイスミスが冬に室内でできる運動として考えた。
facts.easy: Basketball was made in 1891 by a teacher who wanted a sport to play inside in winter.
facts.std: Basketball was invented in 1891 by physical education teacher James Naismith as an indoor game for the winter months.

facts.ja: 19世紀のボクシングでは、ラウンドの数に決まりがなく、どちらかが続けられなくなるまで試合が続いた。
facts.easy: In the 1800s, a boxing match could go on until one fighter could not go on.
facts.std: Under 19th-century bare-knuckle rules, boxing matches had no set number of rounds and continued until one fighter could not go on.

facts.ja: マラソンの42.195kmは、1908年のロンドン五輪で、ウィンザー城からスタジアムのロイヤルボックス前までのコースにしたことから決まった。
facts.easy: The marathon became 42.195 km long at the 1908 London Olympics because of where the race started and ended.
facts.std: The marathon's 42.195 km distance comes from the 1908 London Olympics, where the course ran from Windsor Castle to the royal box in the stadium.

facts.ja: ゴルフボールのくぼみ（ディンプル）は空気の流れを変え、つるつるのボールよりずっと遠くまで飛ばす。
facts.easy: The small holes on a golf ball help it fly much farther than a smooth ball.
facts.std: The dimples on a golf ball change how air flows around it, letting it fly much farther than a smooth ball.

facts.ja: 大相撲の番付は18世紀半ばから続く、とても歴史の長いランキングのしくみ。
facts.easy: Sumo has used the same kind of ranking list for more than 250 years.
facts.std: Sumo's banzuke ranking list dates back to the mid-18th century, making it one of the oldest sports rankings in use.

facts.ja: アメフトの「ハドル」は、19世紀末にろう者の大学のチームが、相手に手話を見られないように始めたとされる。
facts.easy: In American football, players stand in a circle to plan. This may have started at a school for deaf students, so other teams could not see their signs.
facts.std: The football huddle is said to have begun at Gallaudet University, a school for deaf students, so opponents could not read their sign language.

facts.ja: スキーは数千年前の北ヨーロッパで、狩りや移動のために使われていた。スポーツとして広まったのは19世紀。
facts.easy: People in the north of Europe used skis thousands of years ago to hunt and travel. Skiing became a sport in the 1800s.
facts.std: Skis were used for hunting and travel in northern Europe thousands of years ago; skiing became a sport only in the 19th century.

facts.ja: マイケル・フェルプスは2008年北京五輪で金メダルを8個とった。1大会での最多記録。
facts.easy: Michael Phelps won eight gold medals at the 2008 Olympics. No one has won more at one Games.
facts.std: Michael Phelps won eight gold medals at the 2008 Beijing Olympics, the most ever at a single Games.

facts.ja: 大リーグの試合球は、試合の前に特別な川の泥をすりこんで、すべりにくくしている。
facts.easy: Before a baseball game in the US, each ball is rubbed with special mud from a river.
facts.std: Before every Major League Baseball game, the balls are rubbed with a special mud from a river in New Jersey to reduce their shine.

facts.ja: 円周率πは終わりなく続く数。これまでに小数点以下100兆けた以上が計算されている。
facts.easy: Pi is a number that never ends. Computers have worked out more than 100 trillion numbers after the point.
facts.std: Pi is an irrational number whose digits never end; computers have calculated it to more than 100 trillion decimal places.

facts.ja: 数としての「0」を使う考え方は、7世紀ごろのインドで整えられ、アラビアを通ってヨーロッパに伝わった。
facts.easy: The idea of zero as a number came from India and later went to Europe through the Arab world.
facts.std: Zero as a number in its own right was developed in India around the 7th century and reached Europe through the Arab world.

facts.ja: フィボナッチ数列（1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13…）は、ひまわりの種の並びなど、自然の中によく現れる。
facts.easy: The numbers 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13 are called the Fibonacci numbers. You can find them in many plants, like sunflowers.
facts.std: The Fibonacci sequence (1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13...) appears often in nature, such as in the spiral patterns of sunflower seeds.

facts.ja: 「誕生日のパラドックス」：23人集まれば、同じ誕生日の2人がいる確率は50%を超える。
facts.easy: If there are 23 people in a room, there is a better than even chance that two of them have the same birthday.
facts.std: In a group of just 23 people, there is more than a 50% chance that two share a birthday, the so-called birthday paradox.

facts.ja: 無限にも「大きさ」の違いがある。実数の無限は、自然数の無限より大きい（カントール）。
facts.easy: Some kinds of 'never ending' are bigger than others. A mathematician named Cantor showed this.
facts.std: Georg Cantor showed that some infinities are larger than others: there are more real numbers than natural numbers.

facts.ja: コンピューターは0と1だけの2進法で計算する。2進法を詳しく研究したのは17〜18世紀のライプニッツ。
facts.easy: Computers work using only 0 and 1. A thinker named Leibniz wrote about this way of counting long ago.
facts.std: Computers calculate using binary, just 0s and 1s, a number system studied in depth by Gottfried Leibniz around 1700.

facts.ja: 「フェルマーの最終定理」は350年以上だれにも証明できなかったが、1995年にアンドリュー・ワイルズが証明を完成させた。
facts.easy: A famous math problem waited more than 350 years for an answer. Andrew Wiles solved it in 1995.
facts.std: Fermat's Last Theorem remained unproven for over 350 years until Andrew Wiles completed his proof in 1995.

facts.ja: バタフライ効果：最初のわずかな違いが、天気のような複雑なしくみでは大きな違いになる。天気予報に限界がある理由のひとつ。
facts.easy: In weather, a very small change can lead to a very big change later. This is why weather is hard to know far ahead.
facts.std: In chaotic systems such as the weather, tiny differences in starting conditions grow into huge differences, which limits long-range forecasts.

facts.ja: モンティ・ホール問題：3つのドアから1つ選び、はずれのドアを1つ開けてもらったら、選び直したほうが当たる確率は2/3になる。
facts.easy: In a game with three doors, if one wrong door is opened, you should change your choice. You will win two times out of three.
facts.std: In the Monty Hall problem, switching doors after a losing door is revealed wins two thirds of the time.

facts.ja: インターネットの安全を守る暗号の多くは、大きな数を素数に分けるのが難しいことを利用している。
facts.easy: Much of the safety on the internet depends on special numbers called prime numbers.
facts.std: Much internet security relies on public-key cryptography, which depends on how hard it is to break large numbers into prime factors.

facts.ja: 「ケーニヒスベルクの橋」の問題（1736年）を考えたことから、オイラーはグラフ理論の土台を作った。
facts.easy: A puzzle about seven bridges in an old city led Euler to start a new kind of math.
facts.std: Leonhard Euler's 1736 solution to the Seven Bridges of Königsberg puzzle laid the foundations of graph theory.

facts.ja: √2が分数で表せないことを明かしたピタゴラス派の学者ヒッパソスが、海で死んだという伝説がある。
facts.easy: There is an old story that a Greek thinker died at sea because he told a secret about a number.
facts.std: Legend says Hippasus, a Pythagorean, drowned at sea after revealing that the square root of 2 cannot be written as a fraction.

facts.ja: ロシアは世界最大の国で、日本の約45倍の広さ。11の時間帯があり、東と西の端では10時間の時差がある。
facts.easy: Russia is the biggest country in the world. It is about 45 times as big as Japan and has 11 time zones.
facts.std: Russia, the world's largest country, is about 45 times the size of Japan and spans 11 time zones.

facts.ja: インドネシアは約1万7000の島からなる。人口は世界4位。
facts.easy: Indonesia is made up of about 17,000 islands. It has the fourth most people in the world.
facts.std: Indonesia consists of about 17,000 islands and has the world's fourth-largest population.

facts.ja: マリアナ海溝の最も深い所（チャレンジャー海淵）は約1万900m。エベレストを沈めても2000mほど余る。
facts.easy: The deepest part of the sea is about 11,000 meters deep. Even Mount Everest would be under water there.
facts.std: The Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench is nearly 11,000 meters deep; Mount Everest would fit inside with about 2,000 meters to spare.

facts.ja: エベレストは、インドのプレートがユーラシアのプレートを押し続けているため、毎年数cmずつ北東へ動いている。
facts.easy: Mount Everest moves a few centimeters every year, because the land under India is still pushing into Asia.
facts.std: Mount Everest shifts a few centimeters each year as the Indian plate keeps pushing into the Eurasian plate.

facts.ja: 南極の氷がすべてとけると、世界の海面は約58m上がると推定されている。
facts.easy: If all the ice on Antarctica melted, the sea would rise by about 58 meters.
facts.std: If all of Antarctica's ice melted, global sea level would rise by about 58 meters.

facts.ja: サハラ砂漠は世界最大の暑い砂漠だが、砂におおわれているのは一部だけ。多くは岩や小石の大地。
facts.easy: The Sahara is the biggest hot desert in the world. But most of it is rock and stones, not sand.
facts.std: The Sahara is the largest hot desert on Earth, yet only about a quarter of it is covered by sand; most is rock and gravel.

facts.ja: 日本の国土の広さは世界60位前後だが、排他的経済水域（EEZ）は世界でも上位の広さがある。
facts.easy: Japan is not a very big country, but the sea area it controls is one of the biggest in the world.
facts.std: Japan ranks only around 60th in land area, but its exclusive economic zone at sea is among the largest in the world.

facts.ja: 東京を中心とする首都圏の人口は約3700万人。長く世界最大の都市圏とされてきた。
facts.easy: About 37 million people live in and around Tokyo. For many years it was called the biggest city area in the world.
facts.std: Greater Tokyo is home to about 37 million people and has long been ranked the world's most populous metropolitan area.

facts.ja: 地球の淡水の約7割は氷河や氷床として凍っている。すぐに使える淡水は、地球の水全体の1%にも満たない。
facts.easy: Most of the Earth's fresh water is ice. Less than one percent of all water is fresh water we can easily use.
facts.std: About 70% of Earth's fresh water is locked in ice, and less than 1% of all water on the planet is fresh water readily available to us.

facts.ja: アイスランドは国土の約1割が氷河におおわれているが、活火山もたくさんある。「火と氷の国」と呼ばれる。
facts.easy: Iceland has a lot of ice and also many active volcanoes. People call it the land of fire and ice.
facts.std: About a tenth of Iceland is covered by glaciers, yet the island also has many active volcanoes, earning it the name 'land of fire and ice'.

facts.ja: アフリカ大陸は、アメリカ・中国・インドを合わせたより広い。よく使われる地図では実際より小さく見える。
facts.easy: Africa is bigger than the US, China and India put together. Many maps make it look smaller than it is.
facts.std: Africa is larger than the United States, China and India combined, but the common Mercator map makes it look much smaller.

facts.ja: 日本の海岸線は約3万kmあり、世界でも有数の長さ。たくさんの島があるため。
facts.easy: Japan has about 30,000 km of coast because it has so many islands.
facts.std: Thanks to its thousands of islands, Japan has about 30,000 km of coastline, one of the longest in the world.

facts.ja: ベートーヴェンは、ほとんど耳が聞こえなくなってから交響曲第9番を作曲した。
facts.easy: Beethoven wrote his Ninth Symphony when he could hardly hear at all.
facts.std: Beethoven composed his Ninth Symphony when he was almost completely deaf.

facts.ja: モーツァルトは5歳で作曲を始め、35歳で亡くなるまでに600曲以上を残した。
facts.easy: Mozart began to write music at five. He wrote more than 600 works before he died at 35.
facts.std: Mozart began composing at five and wrote more than 600 works before his death at the age of 35.

facts.ja: モナ・リザはたて77cm、よこ53cmの小さな絵。実物を見て小ささに驚く人が多い。
facts.easy: The Mona Lisa is only 77 cm tall. Many visitors are surprised that it is so small.
facts.std: The Mona Lisa measures just 77 by 53 centimeters, and many visitors are surprised by how small it is.

facts.ja: ピカソは一生で約5万点の作品を作った（絵、彫刻、陶器、版画などを含む）。
facts.easy: Picasso made about 50,000 works of art in his life.
facts.std: Picasso produced an estimated 50,000 works in his lifetime, including paintings, sculptures, ceramics and prints.

facts.ja: ピアノの正式な名前は「ピアノフォルテ（弱く・強く）」。音の強弱をつけられるのが新しかった。
facts.easy: The piano's full name is 'pianoforte', which means 'soft-loud'. It could play both soft and loud.
facts.std: The piano's original name, pianoforte, means 'soft-loud' in Italian, because it could play at different volumes.

facts.ja: ジャズは19世紀末から20世紀初めに、ニューオーリンズのアフリカ系アメリカ人の社会から生まれた。
facts.easy: Jazz began in New Orleans in the African American community about 100 years ago.
facts.std: Jazz emerged in the African American communities of New Orleans in the late 19th and early 20th centuries.

facts.ja: バッハの作品は死後しばらく忘れられていたが、1829年にメンデルスゾーンがマタイ受難曲を演奏して再び注目された。
facts.easy: After Bach died, many people forgot his music. It became popular again in 1829.
facts.std: Bach's music fell out of fashion after his death until Mendelssohn revived the St Matthew Passion in 1829.

facts.ja: ゴッホが生きている間に売れた絵は1枚だけという話が有名だが、実際にはほかにも売れていたという研究がある。
facts.easy: People often say Van Gogh sold only one painting in his life. But he may have sold a few more.
facts.std: It is often said Van Gogh sold only one painting during his life, but research suggests he sold a few others.

facts.ja: 映画は1秒間に24コマの速さで撮影・上映するのが長年の標準。
facts.easy: Most films show 24 pictures every second.
facts.std: For about a century, the standard frame rate for cinema has been 24 frames per second.

facts.ja: モネやルノワールら印象派の画家は公式の展覧会（サロン）になかなか選ばれず、1874年に自分たちで展覧会を開いた。
facts.easy: The official art show in Paris did not like Monet and his friends. So in 1874, they made their own show.
facts.std: Rejected by the official Paris Salon, Monet, Renoir and other Impressionists organized their own exhibition in 1874.

facts.ja: 日本の浮世絵は、モネやドガなどヨーロッパの画家に大きな影響を与えた（ジャポニスム）。
facts.easy: Japanese woodblock pictures had a big effect on painters in Europe, like Monet.
facts.std: Japanese ukiyo-e prints strongly influenced European painters such as Monet and Degas, a trend known as Japonisme.

facts.ja: 英語で最もよく使われる文字は「E」で全体の約13%。「Z」は0.1%にも満たない。
facts.easy: E is the most used letter in English. Z is one of the least used.
facts.std: E is the most common letter in English, about 13% of all letters, while Z accounts for less than 0.1%.

facts.ja: set は英語の中でも特に意味の多い単語。辞書を引くと「置く」「決める」「沈む」「一式」など、数十もの意味が並ぶ。
facts.easy: The word set has a lot of meanings. A dictionary lists many, like put, decide and a group of things.
facts.std: 'Set' is one of the English words with the most meanings, from 'put' and 'decide' to 'a group of things' and the sun going down.

facts.ja: 英語の petrichor（ペトリコール）は、雨が降ったあとの土のにおいを表すことば。
facts.easy: 'Petrichor' is the nice smell of the ground after rain.
facts.std: 'Petrichor' is the earthy smell produced when rain falls on dry soil.

facts.ja: typewriter は、キーボードのいちばん上の文字の列だけで打てる、長めの英単語として有名。
facts.easy: You can type the word 'typewriter' using only the top row of letters on a keyboard.
facts.std: 'Typewriter' is a famously long word that can be typed using only the top row of a QWERTY keyboard.

facts.ja: stewardesses（12文字）は、キーボードの左手側のキーだけで打てる長い英単語。
facts.easy: You can type 'stewardesses' with only your left hand on a normal keyboard.
facts.std: 'Stewardesses', with 12 letters, can be typed using only the left-hand side of a QWERTY keyboard.

facts.ja: 英語は約60の国と地域で公用語になっている。
facts.easy: English is an official language in about 60 countries.
facts.std: English is an official language in around 60 sovereign states and many other territories.

facts.ja: rhythm は a, e, i, o, u を1つも使わない英単語。
facts.easy: The word 'rhythm' does not use the letters a, e, i, o or u.
facts.std: 'Rhythm' is one of the longest common English words that contains none of the vowels a, e, i, o or u.

facts.ja: goodbye は「God be with you（神があなたとともにありますように）」が縮まってできたことば。
facts.easy: 'Goodbye' comes from 'God be with you'.
facts.std: 'Goodbye' is a shortened form of the old phrase 'God be with you'.

facts.ja: sandwich は、イギリスのサンドイッチ伯爵の名前から来た。トランプを続けながら食べるために頼んだという話がある。
facts.easy: The sandwich is named after the Earl of Sandwich. The story says he ate it so he could keep playing cards.
facts.std: The sandwich is named after the 4th Earl of Sandwich, who, according to legend, asked for meat between bread so he could keep playing cards.

facts.ja: panic（パニック）は、ギリシャ神話の牧神パンに由来する。パンが起こす突然の恐怖を表した。
facts.easy: The word 'panic' comes from Pan, a Greek god who could make people suddenly afraid.
facts.std: 'Panic' comes from Pan, the Greek god of the wild, who was believed to cause sudden fear.

facts.ja: 世界には約7000の言語があり、その多くが話す人を失いつつある。今世紀中に半分近くが消えるという予測もある。
facts.easy: There are about 7,000 languages in the world. Many of them may stop being used this century.
facts.std: About 7,000 languages are spoken today, and some experts predict that nearly half could disappear by the end of this century.

facts.ja: ハングルは15世紀に朝鮮の世宗大王が学者たちと作った文字で、とても規則的なつくりをしている。
facts.easy: The Korean letters, Hangul, were made in the 1400s by King Sejong and his team. They are very easy to learn.
facts.std: Hangul, the Korean alphabet, was created in the 15th century under King Sejong and is known for its logical design.

facts.ja: 日本語の「木漏れ日」や「わびさび」のように、英語に1語で訳せないことばはたくさんある。
facts.easy: Some Japanese words, like 'komorebi', have no one English word with the same meaning.
facts.std: Japanese words such as 'komorebi', sunlight filtering through leaves, have no single-word equivalent in English.

facts.ja: クラッシェンの「インプット仮説」：今の力より少しだけ難しい内容（i+1）にたくさん触れることで言語が身につくという考え。
facts.easy: One idea says we learn a language best by reading and hearing things that are just a little hard for us.
facts.std: Stephen Krashen's input hypothesis holds that we acquire language by understanding input slightly beyond our current level, which he called 'i+1'.

facts.ja: 2つの言語を長く使ってきた人は、認知症の症状が出るのが平均4〜5年遅いという研究がある。
facts.easy: Some studies found that people who use two languages show signs of memory illness a few years later.
facts.std: Some studies found that lifelong bilinguals showed symptoms of dementia about four to five years later than monolinguals.

facts.ja: 学んだあとに眠ると、その記憶が定着しやすくなることが多くの研究で示されている。
facts.easy: Sleep after study helps you keep what you learned.
facts.std: Many studies show that sleeping after learning helps consolidate new memories.

facts.ja: テスト効果：読み返すより、思い出す練習をしたほうが長く記憶に残る。
facts.easy: Testing yourself helps you remember better than reading again.
facts.std: The testing effect: practicing recall helps you remember far better over time than simply rereading.

facts.ja: 外国語で考えると、感情に流されにくく、より合理的な判断をしやすくなるという研究がある。
facts.easy: One study found that people make calmer choices when they think in a second language.
facts.std: Research suggests people make more rational decisions when thinking in a foreign language, a phenomenon called the foreign-language effect.

facts.ja: エッフェル塔は、夏の暑さで鉄がのびて最大15cmほど高くなる。
facts.easy: The Eiffel Tower can grow up to 15 cm taller in summer, because heat makes the metal longer.
facts.std: The Eiffel Tower can grow up to about 15 cm taller in summer as its iron expands in the heat.

facts.ja: 空が青いのは、太陽の光のうち青い光が空気でより多く散らばるため（レイリー散乱）。夕焼けが赤いのも同じしくみ。
facts.easy: The sky is blue because the air spreads out blue light more than other colors. The same thing makes sunsets red.
facts.std: The sky looks blue because air scatters short blue wavelengths of sunlight more than red ones, called Rayleigh scattering; the same effect makes sunsets red.

facts.ja: 「Buffalo buffalo Buffalo buffalo buffalo buffalo Buffalo buffalo.」は文法的に正しい英文。
facts.easy: 'Buffalo buffalo Buffalo buffalo buffalo buffalo Buffalo buffalo' is a real English sentence.
facts.std: 'Buffalo buffalo Buffalo buffalo buffalo buffalo Buffalo buffalo' is a grammatically correct English sentence, using the city, the animal and the verb.

facts.ja: 辞書にのる最も長い英単語のひとつ pneumonoultramicroscopicsilicovolcanoconiosis は45文字。肺の病気の名前。
facts.easy: One of the longest words in English dictionaries has 45 letters. It is the name of a lung illness.
facts.std: Pneumonoultramicroscopicsilicovolcanoconiosis, a 45-letter word for a lung disease, is one of the longest words in major English dictionaries.

facts.ja: 地球に1時間で届く太陽のエネルギーは、人類が1年間に使うエネルギーより多い。
facts.easy: The sun gives the Earth more energy in one hour than all people use in one year.
facts.std: The solar energy reaching Earth in a single hour is more than all of humanity uses in a year.

facts.ja: 約50億年後、太陽は赤色巨星になって大きくふくらみ、地球をのみこむ可能性もある。
facts.easy: In about five billion years, the sun will grow very big. It may even swallow the Earth.
facts.std: In about five billion years the Sun will swell into a red giant and may engulf Earth.

facts.ja: 砂は無限にあるわけではない。建設に使える角ばった砂が足りなくなり、取り合いが起きている地域もある。
facts.easy: We are running out of the right kind of sand for building. In some places, people fight over it.
facts.std: Sand suitable for construction is becoming scarce, and illegal sand mining has led to conflict in some regions.

facts.ja: 音楽を聞くと、ことば・動き・感情などにかかわる脳のいくつもの場所が同時に働く。
facts.easy: When you listen to music, many parts of your brain work at the same time.
facts.std: Listening to music activates many brain regions at once, including areas for language, movement and emotion.

facts.ja: 1gの土には数億〜数十億個の細菌がすんでいる。
facts.easy: A small spoon of soil can hold hundreds of millions of very small living things.
facts.std: A single gram of soil can contain hundreds of millions to billions of bacteria.

facts.ja: 宇宙全体を満たす「宇宙マイクロ波背景放射」の温度は約−270℃。絶対零度よりわずか2.7度高いだけ。
facts.easy: The light left over from the start of the universe is very cold, only 2.7 degrees above the coldest possible temperature.
facts.std: The cosmic microwave background, the afterglow of the Big Bang, has a temperature of just 2.7 degrees above absolute zero, about minus 270°C.

facts.ja: 地球の中心（内核）の温度は約5200℃で、太陽の表面とほぼ同じくらい熱い。
facts.easy: The center of the Earth is about as hot as the surface of the sun.
facts.std: Earth's inner core is about 5,200°C, roughly as hot as the surface of the Sun.

facts.ja: 宇宙にある原子の約9割は水素、残りのほとんどはヘリウム。そのほかの元素をすべて合わせても1%ほどしかない。
facts.easy: Most atoms in space are hydrogen. Almost all the rest are helium.
facts.std: About 90% of the atoms in the universe are hydrogen and most of the rest are helium; all other elements together make up only around 1%.

facts.ja: ウイルスが生き物かどうかは今も議論がある。自分だけでは増えられず、他の生き物の細胞を使って増えるため。
facts.easy: Scientists still argue about whether viruses are alive. They can only make copies of themselves inside other living cells.
facts.std: Whether viruses count as living things is still debated, because they can reproduce only inside the cells of another organism.

facts.ja: ブラックホールの中心（特異点）では、今の物理学の法則がうまく当てはまらなくなる。
facts.easy: At the center of a black hole, our rules of science stop working.
facts.std: At the singularity at the heart of a black hole, our current laws of physics, including general relativity, break down.

facts.ja: 周期表の118の元素のうち、自然界で見つかるのは約94。残りは研究所で人工的に作られた。
facts.easy: There are 118 known elements. About 94 are found in nature, and people made the rest in labs.
facts.std: Of the 118 known chemical elements, about 94 occur naturally; the rest have only been made in laboratories.

facts.ja: 地球で見つかった最も古い鉱物の粒は約44億年前のもの。月の石には約45億年前のものもある。
facts.easy: The oldest small piece of rock found on Earth is about 4.4 billion years old.
facts.std: The oldest known mineral grains on Earth, zircons from Australia, are about 4.4 billion years old, and some Moon rocks are even older.

facts.ja: 空気は私たちの体をいつも強い力で押している。大人の体全体で約15トン分の力になるが、体の中からも同じ力で押し返しているので感じない。
facts.easy: The air is always pushing on your body very hard. You do not feel it, because your body pushes back just as hard.
facts.std: Air pressure pushes on an adult's body with a total force of around 15 tonnes, but we don't feel it because the pressure inside the body balances it.

facts.ja: さなぎの中で体がほとんど作り直されても、幼虫のときに覚えたことがチョウ（ガ）になっても残っていたという研究がある。
facts.easy: A study found that some insects remember things they learned as young insects, even after they change their whole body.
facts.std: A 2008 study found that moths could remember what they had learned as caterpillars, even after metamorphosis rebuilt their bodies.

facts.ja: ハヤブサは急降下するとき時速380kmを超え、地球上で最も速い動物とされる。
facts.easy: A peregrine falcon can fly down at more than 380 km an hour. It is the fastest animal on Earth.
facts.std: The peregrine falcon can exceed 380 km per hour in a hunting dive, making it the fastest animal on Earth.

facts.ja: ゾウは足の裏で地面を伝わる低い振動を感じ取り、遠くにいる仲間の声に気づくことができると考えられている。
facts.easy: Elephants may 'hear' with their feet. They can feel very low sounds from other elephants through the ground.
facts.std: Elephants can detect low-frequency rumbles from distant herd members through the ground, sensing the vibrations with their feet.

facts.ja: 木の体のほとんどは、土からではなく空気中の二酸化炭素と水から作られている。
facts.easy: A tree is not made mostly from soil. It is made mostly from air and water.
facts.std: Most of a tree's mass comes not from the soil but from carbon dioxide in the air and water, combined through photosynthesis.

facts.ja: イルカは脳の半分ずつ眠り、もう半分で泳ぎや呼吸を続ける。グンカンドリのように飛びながら眠る鳥もいる。
facts.easy: Dolphins sleep with half of their brain at a time. The other half keeps them swimming and breathing.
facts.std: Dolphins sleep with one half of the brain at a time, so they can keep swimming and breathing; some birds, like frigatebirds, sleep this way in flight.

facts.ja: コウイカは色を見分けられないと考えられているのに、周りの色にそっくり合わせて姿を隠せる。そのしくみはまだよく分かっていない。
facts.easy: Cuttlefish probably cannot see colors, but they can change their color to match what is around them.
facts.std: Cuttlefish are thought to be colorblind, yet they blend into their surroundings with remarkable accuracy, and scientists are still working out how.

facts.ja: アリは1匹ずつは簡単なルールで動くだけなのに、群れ全体では複雑で賢い行動ができる。この考え方はロボットやAIの研究にも使われる。
facts.easy: Each ant follows simple rules, but together, ants can do very smart things. People use this idea in computer science.
facts.std: Individual ants follow simple rules, yet colonies solve complex problems together, an example of swarm intelligence that inspires computer algorithms.

facts.ja: 植物は虫に食べられると、においの成分を出して、近くの植物に危険を知らせることがある。
facts.easy: When insects eat a plant, it can send out a smell that warns other plants nearby.
facts.std: When attacked by insects, some plants release airborne chemicals that can prompt neighboring plants to prepare their defenses.

facts.ja: サンゴは動物で、体の中に小さな藻がすんでいる。藻が光合成で栄養を分け、水温が上がって藻が出ていくとサンゴは白くなる（白化）。
facts.easy: Coral is an animal. Tiny plants live inside it and give it food. When the sea gets too warm, they leave and the coral turns white.
facts.std: Corals are animals that host tiny algae in their tissues; when the water gets too warm the algae leave, and the coral turns white, which is called bleaching.

facts.ja: イエローストーン国立公園にオオカミが戻ったことで、シカの行動が変わり、川辺の植物が回復したといわれる。ただし影響の大きさには議論もある。
facts.easy: When wolves came back to a national park in the US, the deer changed how they lived. This helped plants by the rivers grow again.
facts.std: After wolves were reintroduced to Yellowstone, changes in elk behavior are said to have helped riverside plants recover, though scientists debate how large the effect was.

facts.ja: 古代ローマのコロッセオは西暦80年に完成し、5万人以上の観客が入れたと考えられている。
facts.easy: The Colosseum in Rome was finished in the year 80. More than 50,000 people could watch shows there.
facts.std: Completed in AD 80, the Colosseum in Rome could hold an estimated 50,000 or more spectators.

facts.ja: 火薬・羅針盤・紙・印刷術は「中国の四大発明」と呼ばれる。火薬は9世紀ごろの唐の時代に生まれ、10世紀には戦いに使われ始めた。
facts.easy: China gave the world four great inventions: gunpowder, the compass, paper and printing.
facts.std: Gunpowder, the compass, papermaking and printing are known as the Four Great Inventions of China; gunpowder was discovered around the 9th century.

facts.ja: コロンブスはアジアに着いたと信じたまま亡くなったといわれる。アメリカ大陸の名前は、別の探検家アメリゴ・ヴェスプッチから来ている。
facts.easy: Columbus may have died thinking he had reached Asia. America was named after a different explorer, Amerigo Vespucci.
facts.std: Columbus is thought to have believed until his death that he had reached Asia; the Americas were named after another explorer, Amerigo Vespucci.

facts.ja: ガリレオは地動説を支持したため1633年に有罪とされた。カトリック教会が誤りを公式に認めたのは1992年だった。
facts.easy: In 1633, Galileo was found guilty for saying the Earth goes around the sun. The church said it was wrong only in 1992.
facts.std: Galileo was convicted in 1633 for supporting the idea that Earth orbits the Sun; the Catholic Church formally acknowledged its error in 1992.

facts.ja: ギロチンの名前のもとになったギヨタン医師は、死刑そのものに反対していた。のちに家族は名字を変えたといわれる。
facts.easy: Dr. Guillotin, whose name was given to the guillotine, was against killing people as a punishment. Later, his family changed their name.
facts.std: Dr. Joseph-Ignace Guillotin, after whom the guillotine was named, actually opposed the death penalty; his family later changed their surname.

facts.ja: マチュピチュはスペインの征服者に見つからなかった。1911年にハイラム・ビンガムが紹介して世界に知られたが、地元の人々は前から知っていた。
facts.easy: The Spanish never found Machu Picchu. It became famous in 1911, but local people already knew about it.
facts.std: Spanish conquerors never found Machu Picchu; it became world-famous after Hiram Bingham's visit in 1911, though local farmers had long known it.

facts.ja: バイキングには乱暴なイメージがあるが、アイスランドでは930年に「アルシング」という議会を開き、話し合いで物事を決めていた。
facts.easy: Vikings had meetings to make laws. Iceland started one of the oldest such meetings in the year 930.
facts.std: Though remembered as raiders, Norse settlers founded Iceland's Althing in 930, one of the oldest parliaments in the world.

facts.ja: 1884〜85年のベルリン会議などをきっかけに、ヨーロッパの国々はアフリカを分け合い、多くのまっすぐな国境線が引かれた。
facts.easy: In the 1880s, countries in Europe divided Africa among themselves and drew many straight borders.
facts.std: Following the Berlin Conference of 1884-85, European powers divided Africa among themselves, drawing many borders with little regard for local peoples.

facts.ja: ライト兄弟の初飛行（1903年）から、アポロ11号の月面着陸（1969年）まで、わずか66年しかたっていない。
facts.easy: Only 66 years passed between the first plane flight and the first walk on the moon.
facts.std: Just 66 years separate the Wright brothers' first powered flight in 1903 and the Apollo 11 Moon landing in 1969.

facts.ja: ぼんやりしているときも脳は休んでいない。「デフォルト・モード・ネットワーク」という脳の部分がむしろ活発に働いている。
facts.easy: Your brain is busy even when you are doing nothing. Some parts work more when you are resting.
facts.std: Even when we are idle, the brain stays busy: a set of regions called the default mode network becomes more active when we daydream.

facts.ja: 心臓は1日に7000リットル以上の血液を送り出している。
facts.easy: Your heart moves more than 7,000 liters of blood every day.
facts.std: The heart pumps more than 7,000 liters of blood around the body every day.

facts.ja: 肺の中の小さな袋（肺胞）は数億個あり、広げると約50〜75m²にもなる。
facts.easy: Your lungs have hundreds of millions of tiny air bags. Spread out, they would cover a big room.
facts.std: The lungs contain hundreds of millions of tiny air sacs called alveoli, with a total surface area of about 50 to 75 square meters.

facts.ja: 人のゲノム（全遺伝情報）は約30億の文字（塩基対）でできている。
facts.easy: Your genes are written with about three billion 'letters'.
facts.std: The human genome is made up of about three billion base pairs, the 'letters' of DNA.

facts.ja: レム睡眠のとき、脳は起きているときのように活発だが、体の筋肉は力が抜けて動かない。目だけがすばやく動く。
facts.easy: In one stage of sleep, your brain is very busy, but your body cannot move. Only your eyes move fast.
facts.std: During REM sleep the brain is almost as active as when awake, while most muscles are relaxed and still, except for rapid eye movements.

facts.ja: 人の目は約100万色以上を見分けられるとされる。男性の約8%、女性の約0.5%は、特定の色の区別がつきにくい色覚の特徴をもつ。
facts.easy: People can see about a million colors. But about 8% of men find it hard to tell some colors apart.
facts.std: The human eye can distinguish roughly a million colors, but about 8% of men and 0.5% of women have some form of color vision deficiency.

facts.ja: 腸と脳は神経やホルモンでつながっていて、腸内細菌が気分や行動に影響する可能性が研究されている。
facts.easy: Your stomach and your brain talk to each other. Scientists think the small living things in your stomach may change your mood.
facts.std: The gut and brain are linked by nerves and hormones, and researchers are studying how gut bacteria may influence mood and behavior.

facts.ja: 天然痘は、人類が根絶できた唯一の人の感染症（1980年にWHOが宣言）。予防接種のもとを作ったのはジェンナー。
facts.easy: Smallpox is the only human illness people have removed from the world. This was announced in 1980.
facts.std: Smallpox is the only human infectious disease ever eradicated, declared by the WHO in 1980, following vaccination methods pioneered by Edward Jenner.

facts.ja: ピザはイタリア移民によってアメリカに広まり、ニューヨーク風やシカゴ風など、土地ごとに独自のスタイルが生まれた。
facts.easy: Italian people brought pizza to the US. Now cities like New York and Chicago have their own kinds of pizza.
facts.std: Italian immigrants brought pizza to the United States, where regional styles such as New York and Chicago deep-dish developed.

facts.ja: とうがらしの辛さは味ではなく痛みとして感じている。鳥はこの辛さを感じないので、種を遠くまで運んでくれる。
facts.easy: The hot taste of chili is really a feeling of pain. Birds do not feel it, so they eat the seeds and carry them far away.
facts.std: Chili heat is sensed as pain, not taste. Birds can't feel capsaicin, so they eat the peppers and spread the seeds.

facts.ja: オリーブオイルは数千年前から地中海で使われてきた。古代ギリシャの詩人ホメロスは「液体の黄金」と呼んだ。
facts.easy: People around the Mediterranean Sea have used olive oil for thousands of years. A Greek poet called it 'liquid gold'.
facts.std: Olive oil has been used around the Mediterranean for thousands of years; the poet Homer called it 'liquid gold'.

facts.ja: ラーメンは中国の麺料理をもとに日本で独自に発展した。1958年には日清食品が世界初のインスタントラーメンを発売した。
facts.easy: Ramen came from Chinese noodles and changed in Japan. The first instant ramen was sold in 1958.
facts.std: Ramen developed in Japan from Chinese noodle dishes, and in 1958 Nissin released the world's first instant ramen.

facts.ja: チーズは世界に1000種類以上あり、フランスだけでも数百種類がある。
facts.easy: There are more than 1,000 kinds of cheese in the world. France alone has hundreds.
facts.std: There are well over a thousand varieties of cheese worldwide, and France alone produces several hundred.

facts.ja: 緑茶・烏龍茶・紅茶は、すべて同じチャノキの葉から作られる。違いは葉をどれだけ酸化（発酵）させるか。
facts.easy: Green tea, oolong tea and black tea all come from the same plant. They are made in different ways.
facts.std: Green, oolong and black tea all come from the same plant, Camellia sinensis; the difference lies in how much the leaves are oxidized.

facts.ja: バニラはサフランに次いで高価なスパイス。花を手で受粉させる必要があり、世界の生産の多くをマダガスカルが占める。
facts.easy: Vanilla is the second most expensive spice. Each flower must be helped by hand to make fruit.
facts.std: Vanilla is the second most expensive spice after saffron, because its flowers must be pollinated by hand; Madagascar grows most of the world's supply.

facts.ja: 発酵食品は世界中にある。日本の味噌や納豆、韓国のキムチ、ドイツのザワークラウトなど、どの文化にも発酵の知恵がある。
facts.easy: Many cultures have special foods made by small living things, like miso, kimchi and sauerkraut.
facts.std: Fermented foods appear in cultures worldwide, from Japanese miso and natto to Korean kimchi and German sauerkraut.

facts.ja: スポットライト効果：自分の失敗や見た目の変化に、他人は自分が思うほど気づいていない。
facts.easy: Other people notice your mistakes much less than you think.
facts.std: The spotlight effect: we overestimate how much other people notice our mistakes and appearance.

facts.ja: 眠っている間に新しいことを覚えるのは難しい。でも昼に学んだことは、眠っている間に整理されて定着する。
facts.easy: You cannot really learn new things while you sleep. But sleep helps you keep what you learned during the day.
facts.std: Learning brand-new material during sleep is very limited, but sleep plays a key role in strengthening memories formed during the day.

facts.ja: ドーパミンは「快楽の物質」というより、「ごほうびへの期待」や「やる気」にかかわる物質。
facts.easy: Dopamine is more about wanting a reward than enjoying it.
facts.std: Dopamine is linked less to pleasure itself than to anticipating rewards and motivating us to seek them.

facts.ja: メラビアンの法則は「言葉より声や表情が大事」とよく紹介されるが、もとの研究は気持ちと言葉が食い違う場面に限った話。
facts.easy: A famous study about body language is often used in the wrong way. It was only about feelings, not all talk.
facts.std: Mehrabian's often-quoted '7-38-55' rule applies only to situations where words and tone conflict about feelings, not to all communication.

facts.ja: 「成長マインドセット」：能力は努力で伸ばせると考える姿勢。ただし大規模な研究では、介入の効果は小さいという結果もある。
facts.easy: Believing you can get better with work is called a growth mindset. Big studies show it helps only a little.
facts.std: Carol Dweck's 'growth mindset' is the belief that abilities can be developed, though large studies suggest mindset programs have only small effects.

facts.ja: 楽しいときは時間が早く、退屈なときや怖いときは遅く感じる。注意の向け方で時間の感じ方が変わるため。
facts.easy: Time feels fast when you have fun and slow when you are bored or afraid.
facts.std: Time seems to fly when we are enjoying ourselves and to drag when we are bored or frightened, because attention shapes our sense of time.

facts.ja: 初期のコンピューターENIAC（1946年公開）は重さ30トン、真空管1万8000本で、部屋ひとつをうめつくした。
facts.easy: ENIAC, an early computer from the 1940s, weighed 30 tons and filled a whole room.
facts.std: ENIAC, unveiled in 1946, weighed about 30 tonnes, used some 18,000 vacuum tubes and filled an entire room.

facts.ja: インターネットのもとになったARPANETの最初の通信（1969年）では、「LOGIN」と送ろうとして「LO」の2文字でシステムが止まった。
facts.easy: The first message on the early internet in 1969 was meant to be 'LOGIN'. The system stopped after 'LO'.
facts.std: The first message sent over ARPANET in 1969 was supposed to be 'LOGIN', but the system crashed after 'LO'.

facts.ja: 「人工知能（AI）」ということばは、1956年のダートマス会議の提案書から広まった。
facts.easy: The words 'artificial intelligence' became popular after a meeting in 1956.
facts.std: The term 'artificial intelligence' was popularized by the 1956 Dartmouth workshop, often called the birth of AI as a field.

facts.ja: 世界では数十億台のスマートフォンが使われている。初代iPhoneの発売（2007年）から20年足らずで急速に広まった。
facts.easy: Billions of people now use smartphones. They spread very fast after 2007.
facts.std: Billions of smartphones are in use today, most of them adopted in less than two decades after the first iPhone in 2007.

facts.ja: 量子コンピューターが実用化されると、今の暗号の多くが破られるおそれがある。そのため「耐量子暗号」の標準づくりが進んでいる。
facts.easy: Future quantum computers may break much of today's internet safety. People are making new kinds of codes to stop this.
facts.std: Large quantum computers could break much of today's public-key encryption, so new 'post-quantum' standards are being developed.

facts.ja: 遺伝子を狙って書きかえる技術CRISPR-Cas9は「遺伝子のはさみ」と呼ばれ、2020年にノーベル化学賞を受けた。
facts.easy: CRISPR is a tool that can cut and change genes. Its makers won the Nobel Prize in 2020.
facts.std: CRISPR-Cas9, nicknamed 'genetic scissors', earned its developers the 2020 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

facts.ja: 「トロッコ問題」：1人を犠牲にして5人を助けるべきか、という思考実験。自動運転車の判断をめぐる議論でも取り上げられる。
facts.easy: The trolley problem asks: should you hurt one person to save five? People talk about it when they make self-driving cars.
facts.std: The trolley problem, whether to sacrifice one person to save five, is often discussed in debates about how self-driving cars should decide.

facts.ja: サッカーは世界で最も人気のあるスポーツとされ、2022年W杯決勝は約15億人が見たと発表された。
facts.easy: Football is the most popular sport in the world. About 1.5 billion people watched the 2022 World Cup final.
facts.std: Football is widely seen as the world's most popular sport, and FIFA reported that about 1.5 billion people watched the 2022 World Cup final.

facts.ja: 最初のバスケットボールのゴールは本物の桃のかごだった。底があったので、ボールが入るたびにはしごで取り出していた。
facts.easy: The first basketball goals were fruit baskets. Someone had to climb up and take the ball out after each score.
facts.std: The first basketball hoops were real peach baskets with bottoms, so someone had to retrieve the ball after every basket.

facts.ja: テニスで0点を「ラブ」と呼ぶ理由には諸説ある。フランス語の「卵（l'œuf）」から来たという説が有名。
facts.easy: In tennis, zero is called 'love'. One idea says it comes from the French word for egg, because an egg looks like a zero.
facts.std: Nobody is sure why zero is called 'love' in tennis; a popular theory traces it to the French l'œuf, 'egg', for its zero-like shape.

facts.ja: ロープなしでエル・キャピタン（約900mの岩壁）を登りきったアレックス・オノルドは、脳の検査で恐怖にかかわる扁桃体の反応がとても小さかった。
facts.easy: Alex Honnold climbed a 900-meter rock wall with no rope. Tests showed his brain reacts very little to fear.
facts.std: Alex Honnold, who free-soloed El Capitan without ropes in 2017, showed unusually low activity in the brain's fear center, the amygdala, in a scan.

facts.ja: 弓矢は人類の最も古い道具のひとつで、少なくとも数万年前から使われていた。今ではオリンピックの精密なスポーツになっている。
facts.easy: People have used bows and arrows for tens of thousands of years. Today archery is an Olympic sport.
facts.std: Bows and arrows have been used for tens of thousands of years, first for hunting and war and now as a precise Olympic sport.

facts.ja: 記録に残る最初のスキー競技会は、1767年にノルウェーで兵士たちが開いたもの。
facts.easy: The first known ski race was held by soldiers in Norway in 1767.
facts.std: The earliest recorded ski competitions were held by soldiers in Norway in 1767.

facts.ja: ユークリッドの『原論』（紀元前300年ごろ）は、2000年以上も数学の教科書として使われ、「証明」のやり方の手本になった。
facts.easy: A math book written by Euclid about 2,300 years ago was used in schools for more than 2,000 years.
facts.std: Euclid's Elements, written around 300 BC, was used as a mathematics textbook for over two thousand years and set the model for proof.

facts.ja: マンデルブロ集合は z → z²+c という簡単な式のくり返しから生まれる図形。どこまで拡大しても複雑な形が現れる（フラクタル）。
facts.easy: A very simple math rule can make a picture that stays beautiful and complex however close you look.
facts.std: The Mandelbrot set comes from repeating the simple formula z to z squared plus c, yet reveals endless detail at every scale, a famous fractal.

facts.ja: 確率論は、17世紀にパスカルとフェルマーが賭けごとの問題を手紙で話し合ったことから始まった。
facts.easy: The math of chance began when two French thinkers wrote letters about a game of money in the 1600s.
facts.std: Probability theory grew out of letters between Pascal and Fermat in 1654 about how to divide the stakes in an unfinished game of chance.

facts.ja: ゴールドバッハの予想（1742年）「2より大きい偶数はすべて2つの素数の和で書ける」は、まだ証明されていない。
facts.easy: Is every even number bigger than 2 the sum of two prime numbers? No one has proved it yet.
facts.std: Goldbach's conjecture, that every even number greater than 2 is the sum of two primes, has been checked for huge numbers but remains unproven since 1742.

facts.ja: 「p値が0.05未満」は「95%の確率で正しい」という意味ではない。科学者でも誤解していることがある。
facts.easy: A common number in science, the p-value, does not mean 'there is a 95% chance this is true'. Many people get this wrong.
facts.std: A p-value below 0.05 does not mean a result is 95% likely to be true, a misunderstanding common even among scientists.

facts.ja: 「どんな地図も4色あれば、となりあう国を違う色で塗り分けられる」という四色定理は、1976年にコンピューターを使って証明された。
facts.easy: Any map can be colored with only four colors so that no two neighbors are the same. Computers helped prove this in 1976.
facts.std: The four color theorem, proved in 1976, was the first major theorem proved with the help of a computer.

facts.ja: 標高ではエベレストが一番だが、地球の中心から最も遠い山頂はエクアドルのチンボラソ山。地球が赤道でふくらんでいるため。
facts.easy: Everest is the highest mountain. But the top of Chimborazo in Ecuador is the farthest point from the center of the Earth.
facts.std: Everest is highest above sea level, but because Earth bulges at the equator, the summit of Ecuador's Chimborazo is the point farthest from Earth's center.

facts.ja: 太平洋は、地球の陸地をすべて合わせたより広い。
facts.easy: The Pacific Ocean is bigger than all the land on Earth put together.
facts.std: The Pacific Ocean is larger than all of Earth's land area combined.

facts.ja: グリーンランドはほとんどが氷におおわれている。人を呼び寄せるために「緑の土地」と名づけたと、古い物語に書かれている。
facts.easy: Greenland is mostly ice. An old story says it got its name to make people want to live there.
facts.std: Greenland is mostly covered by ice; according to the Norse sagas, Erik the Red named it 'Greenland' to attract settlers.

facts.ja: 富士山は、古い火山の上に新しい火山が重なってできた。最後の噴火は1707年の宝永噴火。
facts.easy: Mount Fuji is made of newer volcanoes on top of older ones. It last blew up in 1707.
facts.std: Mount Fuji is built from several volcanoes stacked on top of each other; its last eruption was the Hōei eruption of 1707.

facts.ja: 太平洋を囲む「環太平洋火山帯」には、世界の活火山の約75%が集まり、地震の約90%が起きている。日本もこの上にある。
facts.easy: Most of the world's earthquakes and many of its volcanoes are around the Pacific Ocean. Japan is in this area.
facts.std: The Pacific 'Ring of Fire' holds about 75% of the world's active volcanoes and sees about 90% of its earthquakes; Japan lies on it.

facts.ja: 砂漠を「雨や雪がとても少ない土地」と考えると、世界最大の砂漠は南極大陸。サハラは「暑い砂漠」として最大。
facts.easy: A desert is a place with very little rain or snow. By that rule, the biggest desert is Antarctica.
facts.std: Because a desert is defined by low precipitation, the largest desert on Earth is Antarctica; the Sahara is the largest hot desert.

facts.ja: モナ・リザには眉毛もまつ毛もないように見える。高解像度の調査で、もとは描かれていた跡が見つかったという報告がある。
facts.easy: The Mona Lisa seems to have no eyebrows. A study found she may have had them, but they faded.
facts.std: The Mona Lisa appears to have no eyebrows, but a high-resolution scan in 2007 reportedly found traces of an eyebrow that had faded.

facts.ja: シェイクスピアの作品が初出とされてきた英単語は多く、bedroom や lonely などもそのひとつ。ただし、もっと古い用例が見つかったものもある。
facts.easy: Many English words, like 'lonely', were first found in Shakespeare's plays.
facts.std: Shakespeare is credited with the first recorded use of many English words, such as 'lonely', though older examples of some have since been found.

facts.ja: 古代ギリシャの彫刻や建物は白い大理石のイメージがあるが、もとはあざやかな色が塗られていた。色は長い年月で落ちた。
facts.easy: Old Greek statues were not always white. Long ago, they were painted in bright colors.
facts.std: Ancient Greek statues and temples, now white marble, were originally painted in bright colors that wore away over time.

facts.ja: 2023年、ビートルズの「最後の新曲」Now and Then が発表された。ジョン・レノンの古い録音からAIを使って声だけを取り出して作られた。
facts.easy: In 2023, the Beatles released one last new song. Computers helped take John Lennon's voice out of an old tape.
facts.std: In 2023 the Beatles released 'Now and Then', using AI-assisted audio separation to lift John Lennon's voice from an old home recording.

facts.ja: バッハの『平均律クラヴィーア曲集』は、指揮者ハンス・フォン・ビューローによって音楽の「旧約聖書」と呼ばれた。
facts.easy: A famous music teacher called one of Bach's piano books the 'Old Testament' of music.
facts.std: Conductor Hans von Bülow called Bach's Well-Tempered Clavier the 'Old Testament' of music.

facts.ja: アメリカ国務省の外交官養成機関は、日本語を英語話者にとって最も習得に時間がかかる言語のひとつに分類している。
facts.easy: For English speakers, Japanese is one of the hardest languages to learn.
facts.std: The US Foreign Service Institute ranks Japanese among the languages that take English speakers the longest to learn.

facts.ja: アルファベットのAは、牛の頭を表すフェニキア文字「アレフ」がもとになっている。
facts.easy: The letter A started as a picture of the head of a cow.
facts.std: The letter A comes from the Phoenician letter aleph, which began as a picture of an ox's head.

facts.ja: ポルトガル語の saudade（サウダージ）は、失ったものや遠くにいる人をなつかしく恋しく思う気持ち。他の言語に1語では訳しにくい。
facts.easy: The Portuguese word 'saudade' means missing someone or something you love. It is hard to say in one English word.
facts.std: The Portuguese word 'saudade' describes a deep, longing nostalgia for someone or something absent, and is famously hard to translate.

facts.ja: スワヒリ語は東アフリカで広く話される共通語。話す人の多くは、第二言語として身につけている。
facts.easy: Many people in East Africa speak Swahili. Most of them learned it as a second language.
facts.std: Swahili is a common language across East Africa, and most of its tens of millions of speakers learned it as a second language.

facts.ja: 相手との関係で言葉を変える敬語は日本語だけのものではない。フランス語の tu と vous、ドイツ語の du と Sie などもその例。
facts.easy: Japanese is not the only language with polite words. French and German also change words to be polite.
facts.std: Many languages mark politeness, not just Japanese: French has tu and vous, and German has du and Sie.

facts.ja: オックスフォード英語辞典の初版は1928年に完成した。作り始めてから70年近くかかり、多くのボランティアが用例を送った。
facts.easy: The first full Oxford English Dictionary took about 70 years to make. Many helpers sent in examples.
facts.std: The first complete edition of the Oxford English Dictionary appeared in 1928, nearly 70 years after work began, with help from thousands of volunteer readers.

facts.ja: 太陽を直径1mの玉にすると、いちばん近い恒星（プロキシマ・ケンタウリ）は約2万9000km先になる。宇宙はそれほどすき間だらけ。
facts.easy: If the sun were a ball one meter wide, the next nearest star would be about 29,000 km away.
facts.std: If the Sun were shrunk to a ball one meter wide, the nearest star, Proxima Centauri, would be about 29,000 km away.

facts.ja: ろうそくの炎の暗い中心部では、ろうの気体がまだ燃えていない。外側の部分が最も温度が高い。
facts.easy: The dark center of a candle flame is not burning yet. The outside of the flame is the hottest part.
facts.std: The dark center of a candle flame is unburned wax vapor; the outer part of the flame is the hottest.

facts.ja: 丸い地球を平らな紙に描くと、どこかが必ずゆがむ。地図は面積・形・距離・方角のどれかを犠牲にしている。
facts.easy: Every flat map is wrong in some way, because the Earth is round.
facts.std: Every flat map distorts something, area, shape, distance or direction, because a sphere cannot be flattened without stretching.

facts.ja: 「6次の隔たり」：世界のだれとでも、知り合いを6人ほどたどればつながるという考え。Facebookの調査では平均3.5人ほどだった。
facts.easy: Any two people may be connected through about six friends. On Facebook, it is only about three or four.
facts.std: 'Six degrees of separation' suggests anyone is linked by about six acquaintances; a 2016 Facebook study found an average of about 3.5.

facts.ja: お札にはたくさんの細菌がついている。アメリカのドル紙幣の調査では3000種類以上の細菌が見つかった。
facts.easy: Paper money has many very small living things on it. One study found more than 3,000 kinds on dollar bills.
facts.std: Banknotes carry many microbes: a study of US dollar bills found DNA from about 3,000 types of bacteria.

facts.ja: 指紋や顔のほかにも、目の虹彩・声・歩き方なども、人を見分ける生体認証に使われている。
facts.easy: Machines can know who you are from your eyes, your voice or even the way you walk.
facts.std: Besides fingerprints and faces, biometric systems can identify people by their irises, voices and even the way they walk.

facts.ja: 1977年に打ち上げられたボイジャー1号は、2012年に太陽圏を出て星間空間に入った。今は地球から250億km近く離れている。
facts.easy: Voyager 1 left Earth in 1977. It is now very far away, in the space between the stars.
facts.std: Voyager 1, launched in 1977, entered interstellar space in 2012 and is now nearly 25 billion kilometers from Earth.

facts.ja: カメレオンの色が変わるのは、皮膚の中にある小さな結晶の並び方が変わり、光の反射が変わるため。
facts.easy: A chameleon changes color by changing very small crystals in its skin.
facts.std: Chameleons change color by adjusting tiny crystals in their skin cells, which changes how light is reflected.

facts.ja: 血液型はABO式だけではない。国際的に認められた血液型の分類は40以上ある。
facts.easy: There are many more blood groups than A, B, AB and O. Scientists know more than 40 systems.
facts.std: ABO is only one of more than 40 recognized blood group systems, many of which matter for safe transfusions.

facts.ja: 2010年にメキシコの伝統料理がユネスコ無形文化遺産に登録された。2013年には「和食」も登録された。
facts.easy: Mexican food became part of world culture to protect in 2010. Japanese food joined in 2013.
facts.std: Traditional Mexican cuisine was added to UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2010, and Japanese washoku followed in 2013.

facts.ja: 8週間のマインドフルネスの練習で、ストレスが減ったり脳の一部に変化が見られたりしたという研究がある。
facts.easy: A study found that eight weeks of quiet attention training helped people feel less stressed.
facts.std: Studies of eight-week mindfulness programs have reported reduced stress and some changes in brain structure, though results vary.

facts.ja: 1956年に登場した最初のハードディスク（IBM 350）は重さ約1トンで、保存できるのは500万文字（約3.75MB）ほどだった。
facts.easy: The first hard disk, from 1956, weighed about a ton. It could hold less than 4 MB.
facts.std: IBM's first hard disk drive, the 350 of 1956, weighed about a tonne and stored only about 3.75 MB.

facts.ja: サーフィンはポリネシアやハワイで古くから行われてきた文化。2020年東京五輪で正式種目になった。
facts.easy: Surfing began long ago in Hawaii and the Pacific islands. It became an Olympic sport in Tokyo.
facts.std: Surfing has ancient roots in Polynesian and Hawaiian culture and became an Olympic sport at the Tokyo 2020 Games.

facts.ja: バチカン市国は面積約0.44km²の世界最小の国。人口は約800人だが、郵便・放送局・鉄道の駅まである。
facts.easy: Vatican City is the smallest country in the world. About 800 people live there, and it even has its own post office.
facts.std: Vatican City, at about 0.44 square kilometers, is the world's smallest country, with roughly 800 residents and its own post office, radio and railway station.

facts.ja: OK の語源として有力なのは、1839年のボストンの新聞が「all correct」をふざけてつづった「oll korrect」の略という説。
facts.easy: 'OK' may come from 'oll korrect', a funny way to write 'all correct' in an 1839 newspaper.
facts.std: 'OK' most likely began as an abbreviation of 'oll korrect', a joking misspelling of 'all correct', in a Boston newspaper in 1839.

facts.ja: 古代オリンピックは紀元前776年から紀元後393年ごろまで、1000年以上続いた。
facts.easy: The Olympic Games in old Greece went on for more than 1,000 years.
facts.std: The ancient Olympic Games were held for more than a thousand years, from 776 BC until about AD 393.

facts.ja: 1950年から2015年までに人類が作ったプラスチックは約83億トン。そのうち約9%しかリサイクルされていないという推定がある。
facts.easy: People have made more than eight billion tons of plastic. Only a small part of it was used again.
facts.std: An estimated 8.3 billion tonnes of plastic were produced between 1950 and 2015, and only about 9% of plastic waste was recycled.

facts.ja: 月には風も雨もないため、宇宙飛行士の足あとは何百万年も残ると考えられている。
facts.easy: There is no wind or rain on the moon. So the footprints there may last for millions of years.
facts.std: With no wind or water on the Moon, astronauts' footprints could last for millions of years.

facts.ja: カタツムリの中には、交尾のときに「恋矢（れんし）」という小さな針を相手に刺す種類がいる。
facts.easy: Some snails shoot a small sharp 'love dart' into their partner.
facts.std: Some land snails stab their mate with a calcium 'love dart' during courtship, which can increase their chances of fathering offspring.

facts.ja: 1977年、電波望遠鏡が宇宙から72秒間の強い信号を受け取った。研究者が記録用紙に「Wow!」と書いたため「Wow!シグナル」と呼ばれ、正体は今も分かっていない。
facts.easy: In 1977, a radio telescope picked up a strong signal from space. A scientist wrote 'Wow!' next to it. No one knows what it was.
facts.std: In 1977 the Big Ear radio telescope recorded a strong 72-second signal; an astronomer wrote 'Wow!' on the printout, and its source remains unknown.

facts.ja: エスペラントは1887年にザメンホフが作った人工言語。国どうしの理解のために考えられ、最も広く話されている人工言語になった。
facts.easy: Esperanto is a language made by one man in 1887. He wanted people from different countries to understand each other.
facts.std: Esperanto, created by L. L. Zamenhof in 1887 to promote international understanding, is the most widely spoken constructed language.

facts.ja: 英語の breakfast は「断食（fast）を破る（break）」から。夜のあいだ食べなかった状態を終える食事という意味。
facts.easy: 'Breakfast' means to 'break' your 'fast'. You have not eaten all night, and this meal ends that.
facts.std: 'Breakfast' literally means breaking the fast of the night, the first meal after hours without food.

facts.ja: company（会社・仲間）はラテン語の「com（いっしょに）＋ panis（パン）」から。もとは「いっしょにパンを食べる仲間」。
facts.easy: The word 'company' first meant people who eat bread together.
facts.std: 'Company' comes from Latin com, 'with', and panis, 'bread': originally, people who share bread.

facts.ja: deadline はもともと、捕虜収容所で越えると撃たれる「死の線」を指した。今は「締め切り」の意味で使われる。
facts.easy: 'Deadline' once meant a line in a prison camp that you must not cross. Now it means the last time to finish work.
facts.std: 'Deadline' originally referred to a line around a prison camp that prisoners could not cross without being shot; today it means a time limit.

facts.ja: budget（予算）は、古いフランス語の bougette（小さな革袋）から。お金を入れる袋が「予算」の意味になった。
facts.easy: The word 'budget' comes from an old French word for a small bag for money.
facts.std: 'Budget' comes from Old French bougette, a small leather bag, from the purse that held money.

facts.ja: salary の語源は塩（sal）、wage は「誓い・保証」、fee は古い英語の「家畜・財産」に関係する。お金の言葉にはそれぞれ歴史がある。
facts.easy: Many money words have long stories. 'Fee' is connected to an old word for farm animals.
facts.std: Money words have deep roots: 'fee' is related to an old Germanic word for livestock, which once served as wealth.

facts.ja: disaster（災害）は「dis（悪い）＋ aster（星）」から。昔の人は、悪い星の並びが不幸を招くと考えた。
facts.easy: 'Disaster' means 'bad star'. People once thought the stars could bring bad luck.
facts.std: 'Disaster' comes from Italian disastro, 'ill-starred', from the old belief that unlucky star positions caused misfortune.

facts.ja: 英語の mortgage（住宅ローン）はフランス語の「死（mort）の誓い（gage）」から。借金を返し終えるか、返せなくなると誓いが「死ぬ」ため。
facts.easy: 'Mortgage' comes from French words that mean 'death promise'. The promise ends when the loan is paid or lost.
facts.std: 'Mortgage' comes from Old French for 'death pledge': the deal 'dies' when the debt is either repaid or the property is lost.

facts.ja: 英語には、ある単語の中に正反対の意味を持つものがある。sanction は「認める」と「制裁」の両方を意味する。
facts.easy: Some English words have two opposite meanings. 'Sanction' can mean 'allow' or 'punish'.
facts.std: Some English words are their own opposites: 'sanction' can mean to approve something or to impose a penalty.

facts.ja: 英語の単語のおよそ3割はフランス語から来たと言われる。1066年にフランスのノルマンディー公がイングランドを征服したことが大きい。
facts.easy: Many English words come from French. This began after a French duke took over England in 1066.
facts.std: A large share of English vocabulary comes from French, much of it after the Norman Conquest of England in 1066.

facts.ja: 英語の pig（豚）は動物の名前で英語由来、pork（豚肉）はフランス語由来。料理を食べる上流階級がフランス語を話していた名残。
facts.easy: 'Pig' is an old English word, but 'pork' comes from French. Rich people who ate the meat spoke French.
facts.std: English uses native words for farm animals (pig, cow) but French-derived words for their meat (pork, beef), a legacy of Norman rule.

facts.ja: 「ド・レ・ミ」の名前は、11世紀の修道士グイードが、聖歌の各行の最初の音節から取ってつけた。
facts.easy: The names do, re, mi come from the first sounds of each line of an old church song.
facts.std: The note names do, re, mi come from an 11th-century hymn: Guido of Arezzo used the first syllable of each line.

facts.ja: 葛飾北斎の「神奈川沖浪裏」は、世界で最もよく知られた日本の絵のひとつ。ゴッホやドビュッシーにも影響を与えた。
facts.easy: Hokusai's picture of a great wave is one of the most famous Japanese pictures in the world.
facts.std: Hokusai's 'The Great Wave off Kanagawa' is one of the world's best-known Japanese artworks and inspired artists such as Van Gogh and composer Debussy.

facts.ja: ジョン・ケージの曲「4分33秒」では、演奏者は楽器を弾かない。聞こえるのは会場のまわりの音だけ。
facts.easy: In John Cage's piece '4′33″', the player does not play any notes. You only hear the sounds in the room.
facts.std: In John Cage's 4′33″, the performer plays nothing; the music is the ambient sound of the room.

facts.ja: ストラディバリが作ったバイオリンは今も約600台残り、1台が十数億円で取引されることもある。
facts.easy: Violins made by Stradivari about 300 years ago can sell for many millions of dollars.
facts.std: About 600 instruments made by Antonio Stradivari survive, and some violins have sold for over ten million dollars.

facts.ja: ミケランジェロはシスティーナ礼拝堂の天井画を約4年かけて描いた。立ったまま上を向いて描いたと考えられている。
facts.easy: Michelangelo spent about four years painting the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel.
facts.std: Michelangelo spent about four years, from 1508 to 1512, painting the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel, mostly standing and looking up.

facts.ja: 人の耳に聞こえる音の高さは、およそ20Hzから2万Hzまで。年を重ねると高い音が聞こえにくくなる。
facts.easy: People can hear sounds from about 20 to 20,000 vibrations a second. As we get older, we hear high sounds less well.
facts.std: Human hearing ranges from about 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz, and the upper limit drops with age.

facts.ja: 近代オリンピックの第1回は1896年にアテネで開かれた。参加したのは男子選手だけだった。
facts.easy: The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens in 1896. Only men took part.
facts.std: The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens in 1896, and only men competed.

facts.ja: バレーボールは1895年、バスケットボールより激しくない室内スポーツとしてアメリカで考えられた。
facts.easy: Volleyball was made in the US in 1895 as a softer indoor sport than basketball.
facts.std: Volleyball was invented in 1895 in the US by William Morgan as a less intense indoor alternative to basketball.

facts.ja: 柔道は1882年に嘉納治五郎が始めた。1964年の東京五輪で正式種目になった。
facts.easy: Judo was started by Kano Jigoro in 1882. It became an Olympic sport at the 1964 Tokyo Games.
facts.std: Judo was founded by Kanō Jigorō in 1882 and became an Olympic sport at the 1964 Tokyo Games.

facts.ja: 男子100mの世界記録はウサイン・ボルトの9秒58（2009年）。最高速度は時速44km台に達したと分析されている。
facts.easy: Usain Bolt ran 100 meters in 9.58 seconds in 2009. No one has run faster.
facts.std: Usain Bolt's 100 m world record of 9.58 seconds, set in 2009, included a top speed of around 44 km per hour.

facts.ja: 卓球は19世紀末のイギリスで、食卓の上で遊ぶ室内遊びとして始まった。ボールの音から「ピンポン」とも呼ばれた。
facts.easy: Table tennis began in England in the 1800s as a game on a dinner table. People called it 'ping-pong' because of its sound.
facts.std: Table tennis began in Victorian England as an after-dinner parlor game, nicknamed 'ping-pong' after the sound of the ball.

facts.ja: 素数は無限にある。このことは2000年以上前にユークリッドが証明している。
facts.easy: There is no biggest prime number. Euclid showed this more than 2,000 years ago.
facts.std: There are infinitely many prime numbers, as Euclid proved more than 2,000 years ago.

facts.ja: 1枚の紙を半分に折り続けると、厚さは折るたびに2倍になる。42回折れれば、計算上は月まで届く厚さになる。
facts.easy: If you could fold a paper 42 times, it would be thick enough to reach the moon.
facts.std: Because thickness doubles with every fold, a sheet of paper folded 42 times would, in theory, be thick enough to reach the Moon.

facts.ja: 「ルービックキューブ」は、どんなに崩れた状態でも20手以内でそろえられることが2010年に証明された。
facts.easy: Any Rubik's Cube can be solved in 20 moves or fewer. This was shown in 2010.
facts.std: In 2010 researchers proved that every position of a Rubik's Cube can be solved in 20 moves or fewer, a number called 'God's number'.

facts.ja: トランプ52枚をよく切ると、その並び方はほぼ確実に歴史上はじめての並びになる。並べ方は約8×10の67乗通りもある。
facts.easy: When you mix a pack of 52 cards well, the order is almost surely new in all of history.
facts.std: A well-shuffled deck of 52 cards is almost certainly in an order never seen before, since there are about 8 × 10^67 possible orders.

facts.ja: 世界で最も長い川はナイル川（約6650km）とされるが、アマゾン川のほうが長いという研究もあり、議論が続いている。
facts.easy: The Nile is often called the longest river. Some studies say the Amazon is longer.
facts.std: The Nile, about 6,650 km, is usually called the world's longest river, though some studies argue the Amazon is longer.

facts.ja: 死海は塩分がとても濃く、人の体は自然に浮く。湖面は海面より約430mも低い。
facts.easy: The water in the Dead Sea is so salty that people float. It is about 430 meters below the level of the sea.
facts.std: The Dead Sea is so salty that swimmers float easily, and its shore is about 430 meters below sea level, the lowest land on Earth.

facts.ja: アマゾンの熱帯雨林は世界の陸上の生き物の種類の約1割がすむと言われる、生物多様性の宝庫。
facts.easy: About one in ten known kinds of land animals and plants live in the Amazon rainforest.
facts.std: The Amazon rainforest is home to roughly 10% of the world's known species.

facts.ja: 琵琶湖は日本最大の湖で、数十万年以上の歴史をもつ世界有数の古い湖。
facts.easy: Lake Biwa is the biggest lake in Japan. It is one of the oldest lakes in the world.
facts.std: Lake Biwa, Japan's largest lake, is also one of the world's oldest lakes, hundreds of thousands of years old.

facts.ja: QRコードは1994年に日本のデンソーウェーブが、自動車部品の管理のために開発した。
facts.easy: The QR code was made in Japan in 1994 to keep track of car parts.
facts.std: The QR code was invented in 1994 by Japan's Denso Wave to track automotive parts.

facts.ja: 絵文字（emoji）は1999年ごろ日本の携帯電話向けに作られ、今では英語の辞書にも emoji として載っている。
facts.easy: Emoji were first made for Japanese mobile phones around 1999. Now 'emoji' is an English word.
facts.std: Emoji were created for Japanese mobile phones in the late 1990s, and the word 'emoji' is now in English dictionaries.

facts.ja: 世界初の携帯電話による通話は1973年。端末の重さは1kg以上あった。
facts.easy: The first mobile phone call was made in 1973. The phone weighed more than one kilogram.
facts.std: The first handheld mobile phone call was made in 1973 by Martin Cooper of Motorola, on a phone weighing over a kilogram.

facts.ja: 新幹線は1964年に開業した世界初の高速鉄道。長年、乗客の死亡事故ゼロを続けている。
facts.easy: The Shinkansen started in 1964. It was the first high-speed train in the world.
facts.std: Japan's Shinkansen, opened in 1964, was the world's first high-speed rail line and has an outstanding safety record.

facts.ja: 「エビングハウスの忘却曲線」：覚えたことは最初の1日で大きく忘れるが、間をあけて復習すると忘れにくくなる。
facts.easy: We forget a lot in the first day after we learn something. Reviewing at good times helps us remember.
facts.std: Hermann Ebbinghaus found that we forget much of what we learn within a day, but spaced review slows forgetting.

facts.ja: 「間隔反復」：同じ時間を使うなら、一度にまとめて覚えるより、日をあけて何度も復習したほうが長く覚えていられる。
facts.easy: It is better to study a little on many days than to study a lot on one day.
facts.std: Spaced repetition, reviewing material at growing intervals, leads to much better long-term memory than cramming.

facts.ja: 新しい習慣が自動的になるまでの日数は人によって大きく違い、ある研究では中央値が約66日だった。
facts.easy: A study found it takes about two months for a new habit to feel natural.
facts.std: One study found that new habits took a median of about 66 days to become automatic, with wide variation between people.

facts.ja: 「もし〇〇したら△△する」と決めておく if-then プランは、目標を行動に移す助けになることが多くの研究で示されている。
facts.easy: Planning 'If this happens, then I will do that' helps people do what they want to do.
facts.std: Research on 'implementation intentions', if-then plans, shows they help people turn goals into action.

facts.ja: 人の体の中で一番大きい細胞は卵子、一番小さい細胞のひとつは精子。
facts.easy: The biggest cell in the human body is the egg cell.
facts.std: The largest cell in the human body is the egg cell, while the sperm cell is among the smallest.

facts.ja: 胃の内側の粘膜は数日ごとに新しく入れかわり、強い胃酸から胃自身を守っている。
facts.easy: The inside of your stomach makes a new cover every few days. This keeps strong acid from hurting it.
facts.std: The stomach lining renews itself every few days, protecting the stomach from its own strong acid.

facts.ja: 人は鼻をつまむと、食べ物の味の多くが分かりにくくなる。「味」と感じているものの多くは、実はにおい。
facts.easy: If you close your nose, much food tastes less clear. A lot of what we call taste is really smell.
facts.std: Much of what we call flavor comes from smell, which is why food tastes bland when your nose is blocked.

facts.ja: カレーライスはインドからイギリスを経て明治時代の日本に伝わり、日本独自の料理として広まった。
facts.easy: Curry came to Japan from India through Britain. It changed into a Japanese dish.
facts.std: Curry reached Japan from India by way of Britain in the Meiji era and developed into a distinct Japanese dish.

facts.ja: とうもろこしのひげ1本1本は、実の1粒1粒につながっている。
facts.easy: Each hair on an ear of corn is connected to one corn seed.
facts.std: Each strand of corn silk is connected to a single kernel; a kernel only develops if its strand is pollinated.

facts.ja: 現存する世界最古級の会社は大阪の金剛組で、578年創業とされる。寺社建築の会社で、四天王寺の建立に関わったと伝えられる。
facts.easy: One of the oldest companies in the world is Kongo Gumi in Osaka. It started in the year 578 and builds temples.
facts.std: Kongo Gumi, an Osaka temple builder said to have been founded in 578, is often cited as one of the oldest continuously operating companies in the world.

facts.ja: 世界で初めて株式を一般に発行した会社の一つは、1602年に設立されたオランダ東インド会社。アムステルダムで株が売買された。
facts.easy: The Dutch East India Company, started in 1602, was one of the first companies to sell shares to the public.
facts.std: The Dutch East India Company, founded in 1602, was among the first companies to issue shares to the public, which were traded in Amsterdam.

facts.ja: 大阪・堂島の米市場では、江戸時代に「将来の米」を売買する取引が行われていた。世界で最初期の先物市場の一つとされる。
facts.easy: In the 1700s, traders in Osaka bought and sold rice for the future. It was one of the first futures markets in the world.
